# Issue #483: Policymaker at the start of iteration 0095

Runs because: every 1 iterations. Change `policy/` and `execution/` where needed; order work in `.session/orders.json`.

Input: `.session/loop-state.json`. Rules: `.session/policymaker.md`. Iteration 0095 waits for you; orders of policy-layer roles start when you finish, and you run again when they end.

---
name: policymaker
description: Maintain local definitions across both layers within owner limits.
startup:
  - .session/policymaker.md
  - .session/loop-state.json

# Policymaker

Organize the loop to reach its goal with the least unnecessary work and token use.
Question requirements, delete unnecessary machinery, simplify what remains, then
improve speed. Revise your own method when evidence calls for it.

## Decide from evidence

Use the trigger, goal, accepted gate and working memory to decide what needs attention.
Find earlier work through `.session/history/manifest.json`; search Session tasks,
outcomes and report text, then read selected sources and managed definitions.
Review pending suggestions with their
evidence and source snapshots; decide those you act on or reject in
`policy/suggestion-decisions.json` (see `.session/policymaker.md`), and leave those needing more evidence pending.

Maintain `policy/working-memory.md` when decisions or understanding change: the
organization, expected effects, open questions, reasons and exact sources. State
which results it considers. Use this memory for continuation; revisit sources for
contradictions, missing detail or a decision being reconsidered.

Handle `.session/startup.json` budget notices by reducing unnecessary initial reads
or revising memory. The owner budget is a warning, including for your own Session.

Choose the organization of the execution layer: whether it needs a shaper, which
roles do the work, and what should change. Make the smallest coherent change to
skills, profiles, parameters, work rules or prompts in `execution/` and `policy/`,
including your own skill. Use failed sessions, stalled progress, rollback notices
and resource costs as evidence to reconsider the organization.

Initially let the shaper maintain `journal/working-memory.md` for execution threads
and reasons. Other roles report findings instead of editing that shared memory.
Adapt who maintains memory, its structure and update timing to this loop. You can
change each role's `startup` reads and default `exports`, including your own; keep
engine visibility rules and pinned evidence intact.

## Start by improving the environment

Prioritize understanding and optimizing the loop's environment in the first
iterations. Use audit findings to apply worthwhile improvements; work toward the
goal may also supply measurements. Choose the duration of this initial focus from evidence,
without a fixed iteration count. Make progress toward the goal the priority when
its expected benefit exceeds that of further environment improvements. Choose later
audit timing and scope from evidence.

## Write roles for this loop

Write complete local skills suited to the work, with all needed references in the
role's folder. Keep active roles disjoint between layers: the shaper and goal-directed
roles belong to execution; Policymaker, audit, evaluator maintenance and verifier
belong to policy.

Use the Skill reference library (https://github.com/mattpocock/skills) when it would
help. Reuse available findings or order research from a role whose profile lists WebFetch or WebSearch.
Write skills inspired by useful findings, rather than copying them.
Research and source reporting are optional.

## Respond to what the loop needs

If the evaluator no longer tracks the goal, order a fix. Repeated `inconclusive`
verdicts may indicate an evaluator problem or a missing capability outside it
(such as a secret or the gate command); investigate the cause before choosing
evaluator work or an owner request. Propose a goal change when the goal itself
needs revision.

Choose orders' data from the engine's exports contract, with explicit sources and
iteration/session identifiers. Check `.session/exports/manifest.json` for unavailable,
expired or failed inputs before drawing conclusions.

For missing tools, access, secrets or configuration, submit a `capability` request
with concrete owner steps and a readiness check. Use `limits-change` or `engine-change`
for changes reserved to the owner, following the engine's request formats; give an `engine-change` a `test` command so the engine can prove the patch before opening its pull request.
Explain what each request unblocks.

## Order the work

Order work as a task graph in `.session/orders.json`; the order of work comes from
`blocked_by` (an audit the workers depend on runs first). Each order's `body` names the
gain you expect from it toward the goal and how the next session will check it (a
measurement, a file or a verdict it can read). An order without an expected gain is
busywork: do not place it. Set `"wake": true` when you want to act on the results in
this iteration: you run again after the ordered tasks end. State the same expectations
for each change in your report.

## Write for the owner in Simplified Technical English

Write each text that the owner reads in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English: the
`title`, `what`, `why` and `unblocks` of each request in `.session/requests.json`, and
`.session/report.md`. The owner must understand the text at first reading, without the
context of your session.

- Use short sentences: at most 20 words in an instruction, 25 in a description.
- Use one idea in one sentence. Use the active voice and the simple present or past tense.
- Use the approved meaning of a word. Use the same word for the same thing every time;
  do not use a synonym. Use the terms of `CONTEXT.md` (for example Owner request,
  Policymaker, Goal gate) and explain no other special term without a concrete example.
- Put the decision first: what the owner must do, or what the owner must decide, then
  the reason. A request has this order: `title` (the action), `what` (the situation and
  the action), `why`, `unblocks` (what starts when the owner acts).
- Write the steps for the owner as a numbered list. One step is one action. Give the
  exact file, command or value.
- Keep the structure and the formatting: headings, lists, and tables stay. Do not make
  the text longer, and do not remove a fact or a link to evidence. Remove only words
  that carry no information.

Do not change `frozen`, `readiness` and `test`. They are exact content that the engine
applies or runs. Do not change a quotation of evidence.

You are the Policymaker. Follow the engine contract supplied in system instructions.

# Policymaker

The trigger and current loop state are in `.session/loop-state.json`.

Read `docs/perpetua/operating-parameters.md` when tuning limits or responding to
stalled work. Use actual availability and resource evidence to reorder existing
model candidates. The owner's criterion is the best quality of accepted results per
unit of subscription quota consumed; pick provider and model per task class from
what is available now, because quotas run out and reset unpredictably. Treat
`docs/perpetua/model-selection.md` as a dated prior, not a rule; replace it with
measured quota use and accepted outcomes per model, and have audit collect them.
Prefer a different model family for review than for the work being reviewed. Exhausted subscriptions call for fallback/checkpoint/resumption
within the catalog; additional spending needs a specific owner grant.

Follow `docs/perpetua/accepted-limits.md` for private data, provider disclosure,
publication and spending. Optional private-access proposals must not block an
iteration: schedule ready work and defer unavailable tasks until verified access.

## POC state and next work
- The bounded unsuccessful POC is delivered and accepted: #477, record 0093, commit d616e38;

  Passing validates failure-delivery consistency only. Original bytes were not rehashed by this offline check.
- Original session artifact from #477: poc-original.vi, 6,371 bytes, SHA256
  cf4b1f56c8e42a7a353101ba1322aa3d64207bb19df5dc791cb3eedf2bb2f7e8;

  162 entries/842 bytes. #473 found no executable recipe after eight VIs. Preserve these sources and pins.
  Primitive identity/replacement, DTHP/VCTP and ConstValue encoding, BDPW's last 32 bytes, and compiled-cache
  invalidation remain unresolved. No disk patch, cache deletion or 103 -> 104 semantic claim is supported.
- Two saved exits: controlled same-version fixture pairs, or missing pinned source rules. They are optional future
  routes, not prerequisites to continued work. Reopen only with a bounded new question and available evidence.
- The next shaper must read delivery.md, record unsuccessful delivery in journal memory, and resume benchmark
  preparation without waiting for owner replies. Current journal is #476's pre-task plan, correctly says pending,

- POC remains the method-first exception, not a product. A future successful demonstration needs a fresh describing/

## Benchmark resumption and gate
- POC delivery ends the POC-only pause. #479 reread `docs/perpetua/evaluation.md`; it does not select benchmark tasks.

- No quota-use measurement exists. Input/cache accounting is not subscription quota use; model labels are not

  No audit ordered now; previous #43/#55 crashed. Keep the current iteration short.
- Read docs/perpetua/accepted-limits.md before private use/disclosure/publication/spending or capability requests.

# Execution working memory

## Considered
- Iteration 0094 startup documents read once: issue, orchestrator skill, loop state, capabilities, previous memory and startup diagnostics (`ok`, estimated 11,994 tokens).
- Loop state: iteration 0093 accepted/improved, one task; checkout identified by `.session/history/manifest.json` as `1d4e33205c9f206c32c700f48fa24bc017dba8af`. Read substantive result directly in `docs/research/poc/delivery.md`.
- Read `.github/loop/task-graph.md`, `docs/perpetua/roles.md`, `evaluation.md` and `operating-parameters.md`; live loop-state parameters supersede dated cadence statements.
- Read `benchmark/preparation-status.json`, `benchmark/protocol.md` and `benchmark/change-cases/README.md`. No files matched `benchmark/writing/**`. A combined-term Grep on protocol returned no matches; the subsequent full Read supplies evidence, not that search result.
- Earlier benchmark and POC details below are inherited pointers unless explicitly noted as read above; not a fresh audit of every linked result.

## State
- Bounded unsuccessful POC is delivered and iteration 0093 accepted. `docs/research/poc/delivery.md` accounts for missing changed VI, missing fresh-agent demonstration, unestablished semantics/version preservation and absent LabVIEW validation; it gives concrete blockers, two exits and owner reproduction instructions. This satisfies the permitted failure-delivery route, not POC success or proof of impossibility.
- POC code/evidence remain under `docs/research/poc/`; no product work is authorized. Eight selected VIs parsed, but no executable semantic edit was supported. Preserve the saved candidates rather than restarting open-ended reverse engineering.
- No session can run LabVIEW. If new controlled evidence later warrants another POC, the describing/editing session must receive a tool and an unseen VI without prior analysis of that VI.
- Benchmark preparation resumes without waiting for owner action. Existing protocol covers read fidelity, answers/source support, controlled-change analysis and paired reading comparisons, but does not explicitly specify creation/modification outcome accounting. Writing-method extension is the selected next useful work; it must build on existing method and change-case designs, not recreate the benchmark.
- `benchmark/preparation-status.json` records scoped reviewed designs, public development examples, zero native executions and unavailable native answers. Its review labels are not benchmark readiness; its long limitations text is more authoritative than shorthand milestone names. Do not change pinned status/index merely to claim writing coverage.
- Split allocator fix #446 still needs independent re-review according to inherited memory. Deferred this iteration to address the goal's explicit writing-method requirement. Before ordering re-review, locate and read actual #446 task/report and pin baseline/candidate trees via `.session/history/manifest.json`; do not infer its review status from stale preparation-status wording.
- Native capability #169 and substantive independent native oracles remain open because structural/public XML checks cannot establish runtime or diagram semantics. Read concrete paused evidence before deciding the next native work. Declined method assessment #430 (`not_planned`) must not be resubmitted unchanged.
- Product implementation remains deferred until independently checked benchmark method/evidence and owner method acceptance; writing implementation additionally needs writing-task coverage. No accepted goal gate exists; owner silence grants nothing.
- All-version effort/compatibility estimate remains open, inherited pointer `docs/research/0002-delivery.md`; writing coverage reportedly missing. Reconcile before choosing LabVIEW 2024 fallback; none selected.

## This iteration
- `.session/tasks.json` orders one benchmark task, `writing-method-extension`, default model/high effort, 120 minutes/65 turns, main, no dependencies, inputs or exports. One bounded authoring session keeps changes disjoint from pinned evidence and avoids premature parallel review.
- Expected gain: `benchmark/writing/README.md`, `method.json`, `verify_method.py` and compact committed verification evidence. Specifications cover creation and modification, independently established expected results, semantic/unrelated-content/save-version preservation, source/rebuild treatment, paired comparisons and honest missing-native outcomes.
- Existing protocol, change-case files, preparation index/status and reviewed evidence must remain byte-identical. No actual edit experiment, writer, product code, runner or evaluator implementation is ordered.
- Verification: `python3 -I benchmark/writing/verify_method.py`; offline/read-only rerun with positive and rejecting synthetic controls and asserted reasons. Passing means specification consistency only, never native or quality success.
- Next cold shaper: read the task report and actual new writing specification/verification evidence. If usable, order a separate reviewer session with exact accepted baseline/candidate trees, protocol and original evidence; do not let the author approve readiness. If incomplete, address the concrete omission without repeating a global gap inventory. Independent review is deliberately left to a later graph once pinned output exists.

## Tried, do not repeat
- #465/#468 established RSRC containers, BDHb decompression and entry framing; see POC README/comparison.json. Framing and endpoint pairs are not primitive semantics.
- #468's in-memory 103 -> 104 mutation was syntactic only; candidate-change.json records no written VI or LabVIEW test. Never treat it as Add-to-Subtract evidence.
- Iteration 0092 inspected eight fixtures and source slices; edit-readiness.md/json retain null recipe and semantic/type/BDPW/cache blockers. Resume only with new bounded evidence, not indiscriminate corpus searches.
- Iteration 0093 delivered the negative POC package. Do not repeat delivery or keep benchmark preparation paused for owner response. No changed VI was fabricated.
- Existing edit-readiness.json pins README/evidence hashes. Add separate documents rather than modifying those dependencies for navigation.
- Do not repeat global gap maps #282/#330/#400, lineage batches without allocation effect or store-readiness reviews without a concrete new question.
- Use path-specific Glob patterns; broad **/* previously truncated. Verification reruns lack LABVIEW_ENVIRONMENT, session artifacts and .session/report.md; rely on small committed evidence and one plain python3 command. Parent commits; no git commit or git-status acceptance requirement.

# Writing method extension

Design only, unreviewed. No artifact has been edited, no agent comparison or LabVIEW job has run, and no native key or benchmark readiness is established. [method.json](method.json) extends the [existing protocol](../protocol.md), [typedef-impact](../change-cases/typedef-impact.spec.json) and [diagram-difference](../change-cases/diagram-difference.spec.json) specifications. The [evaluation contract](../../docs/perpetua/evaluation.md), [role sequence](../../docs/perpetua/roles.md) and [writing goal](../../goal/goal.md#pisanie) remain authoritative. Previously reviewed files, preparation index and milestone status stay at their original bytes.

The [bounded unsuccessful POC](../../docs/research/poc/delivery.md) supplied no executable semantic edit, changed VI, save-version demonstration or runtime check. It is evidence of those limits, never an editor implementation or oracle. Parsing, changed bytes, a successful process, matching selected outputs alone, and owner silence cannot establish writing success.

## Existing obligations and additions

`existing_requirements` E1–E8 records exactly what is inherited, with source lines/anchors: task/provenance records; independent keys and original preservation; derived-copy change recipes; separate answer/grounding/reading measurements; public/private lineage boundaries; paired baselines; positive/rejecting controls; resource and acceptance sequence. `new_requirements` W1–W8 maps each addition back to those obligations: actual artifact outputs, absent creation destinations, frozen semantic/preservation IDs, preserved save versions, separate artifact/native judgments, compiled source/rebuild chains, writing output accounting and artifact-level rejection controls. This extension supplies no replacement protocol or executable scoring policy.

## Task contracts

| Task | Requested artifact result | Independent expected result and current gap |
|---|---|---|
| WC1 | Create `Increment.vi` with I32 `x + 1 -> y`, target save version `21008000`, no state or extra operations | Exact arithmetic vectors and graph obligation derive from the request. Native reference, connector map, documentation pins and separate checking are unavailable. |
| WM1 | Insert one Boolean NOT immediately before the selected output in the original pinned VI from DD-E1 | False/true inversion is specified; original computation, native locators, save version and controlled reference results remain unavailable. DD-E2 is a separate presentation preservation control, not a behavior edit. |
| WM2 | Wrap the pinned typedef root as `original_value` plus Boolean `impact_probe=false`, retaining defaults and typedef mode | Requested cluster semantics are specified. Confirmed consumers, propagation save set, save versions and effects remain unavailable; broken consumers must be reported, never repaired silently. |
| WB1 | Change matched source increment 1 to 2 and rebuild a packed library, retaining exported API and source versions | Exact arithmetic and API obligations are specified. Matching source/build originals, toolchain and native evidence are absent. Source-only work and unexecuted build remain separate; binary patching is excluded. |

Every contract records source/requirement anchors, preconditions, output paths, original hashes where available, semantic IDs, unrelated-content/version invariants, answer IDs and independent oracle provenance requirements. Requirement-derived values are independent of candidate output; they are not claimed as observed LabVIEW results. Before exposure, a separate preparer/checker must freeze original/native object maps, dependency closure, typed fixtures, resets, bounded timeouts, exact comparisons, evidence hashes and per-ID agreement. Unknown locators or versions block eligibility; they cannot be filled from the evaluated agent's output. Native disagreement blocks the affected key.

Artifact fidelity checks the complete output file set, typed objects and relations, intended delta, unrelated objects/files and per-file save version. Correct prose does not rescue a wrong artifact. Answer correctness and original/output source support follow the existing required-ID, extra-claim and contradiction rules separately. Native load, compile/build, controlled execution and hardware/target execution each require their own actual evidence; editing without LabVIEW can produce an artifact while all native outcomes remain unexecuted. No blanket exception permits conversion or unrelated resave changes.

## Paired writing comparison

Reuse the [runner contract](../baseline/runner-contract.md) and [precision plan](../precision/README.md). Freeze a hashed writing addendum to the existing manifest: identical requests, original copies, allowed documentation/images, common prompts, ordinary editing facilities, model/settings and total token/context/output/artifact-byte/wall-time budgets. Only evaluated-tool access differs; its output/time/cost counts against the shared totals. Neither arm receives LabVIEW access in this stratum. Any later native validation is a separate trusted job after both outputs are frozen.

Each repetition uses fresh sessions and dependency-isolated workspaces, deterministic randomized arm order and frozen keys. Four development pilot repetitions is the existing design allocation, conditional on quota; evaluation repetitions remain undecided. Retain every planned slot, failed call, retry, absent/invalid output, actual artifact bytes/hash and unexecuted attempt. Report artifact semantic and preservation results, answers, grounding and native results separately, with fixed denominators and planned/attempted/produced/native-executed/scored/complete-pair counts. The inherited paired lineage-cluster uncertainty procedure and missing-pair bounds extend to separate artifact semantic and preservation fractions; no owner threshold or completed comparison is implied.

Public originals, fixtures and derivatives stay in development lineage groups. None is withheld or demonstrably model-unseen. Future restricted writing cases and keys require commissioned sources, a custodian, actual allocation, tested runner isolation and independent review; store readiness alone supplies none of those. `coverage` lists uncovered families and versions explicitly. All writing runtime counts are zero; 2024 is unverified and no fallback or family reduction is selected.

## Reproducible design check

Run from the repository root:

```text
python3 -I benchmark/writing/verify_method.py
```

The stdlib checker reads only adjacent `method.json` and [controls.json](controls.json), accepts no external input and writes no files. Neither `LABVIEW_ENVIRONMENT` nor `.session/` is needed. It checks fixed task/requirement inventories, required fields, arithmetic/inversion consistency and dimension/coverage declarations, then checks hand-authored fictional graph snapshots against separately stated requirements. There is no LabVIEW parser, writer, benchmark runner or production evaluator.

Positive controls retain creation, modification, source-only modification with unavailable rebuild, and a matched but unexecuted pair. A valid fictional `x+1` graph passes its own request but fails the `x+2` request, exposing a constant writer. Thirty-five in-memory mutations must reject for exact asserted reasons: no-op/changed-bytes-only, wrong graph/type, unintended edits/files, missing output, version drift/unknown version, unsupported artifact, wrong answers/citations/extras, invented native success, overwritten originals, creation overwrite, mismatched pair inputs/budgets, missing arm/accounting, method overclaims and missing fields, missing compiled source, invented rebuild and mismatched source/build linkage. The fixed control inventory prevents silently dropping a rejecting test. This is a bounded contract check, not a complete semantic checker; coordinated edits to fixtures and checker still need independent review.

[verification.json](verification.json) records the actual check and input hashes; [input-pins.json](input-pins.json) records baseline identity and preserved evidence hashes. Passing means design consistency only. Synthetic graph fields are not decoded LabVIEW objects, `SYNTHETIC-v1` is not a real save version, and none of these controls produces native evidence or authorizes measurement.

## Next review and decisions

Give a separate reviewer the parent's pinned candidate commit/tree, baseline `486030b461e57ca0f322a17a5b7853e83e9655e3` / tree `cf75cf6892de2f9410fa09ee2589dcba47d825a4`, output hashes and original-source evidence. Review requirement coverage, expected-result independence, control discrimination and all unavailable outcomes. This task does not seek method acceptance. Later owner/resource decisions remain native authoring/validation capability and grants (#169), matching sources/build tools, independently authored/checked fixtures, restricted allocation and run isolation, model quota/precision targets, and all-version writing effort/compatibility estimates before any fallback. Only after separate review can the owner consider method acceptance before product writing implementation. Executable benchmark scoring belongs to a Policymaker-ordered evaluator change and its separate verifier.

# Ocena początkowa i droga do benchmarku

Stan startowy: **skuteczność narzędzia niezmierzona, benchmark nie istnieje**.
Temat setupu przygotowuje ocenę; nie buduje produktu ani docelowego zestawu przypadków.
Podstawą są ustalenia [niezależnej weryfikacji](https://github.com/Kucze3205/ConnectWithLabview/issues/10#issuecomment-6225343449)
i [dostępu do środowiska](https://github.com/Kucze3205/ConnectWithLabview/issues/2#issuecomment-6248028771).
Kompilacja przykładu VI z 2014 w kontenerze NI 2026 Q1 dowodzi dostępu do tego środowiska,
nie poprawności czytnika, VI Scripting ani obsługi wszystkich wersji. Dostęp 2024 pozostaje niezweryfikowany.

## Co rozstrzyga skrypt, a co właściciel

Zachowano dostarczoną bramkę `gate.kind: owner`. Każda zmiana pracy czeka na decyzję
właściciela; nie zaakceptowano progów jakości ani samodzielnego kończenia celu.
Właściciel ocenia treść dowodów, dopuszcza rozpoczęcie implementacji dopiero po wiarygodnej
metodzie weryfikacji, akceptuje progi sukcesu i ewentualną zmianę zakresu. W temacie D
zaakceptował zasady sukcesu zapisane w `goal/goal.md`: pełny zakres, osobne pomiary
wierności odczytu i odpowiedzi popartych źródłem oraz niezależny benchmark z porównaniem.
Progi jakości i wykonywalna bramka celu czekają na wiarygodny benchmark i osobną
akceptację właściciela; przyszła bramka wymaga `owner_confirms: true`. Plik
`goal/gate.yml` pozostaje nieobecny, więc pętla nie ogłasza samodzielnie sukcesu. Zastąpienie
bramki skryptem wymaga jego decyzji oraz niezależnie sprawdzonej metody. Nie jest to
ograniczenie celu do wersji lub rodzin obecnych w pierwszych przykładach.

`check` uruchamia `python3 policy/evaluator/evaluate.py --check` w kandydacie. Sprawdza
jedynie poprawność opcjonalnego indeksu dowodów: schemat, lokalne ścieżki, niepuste pliki
i SHA256. Brak indeksu jest normalnym stanem początkowym, raportowanym jawnie; błędny
istniejący indeks zatrzymuje zmianę. Ten check nie potwierdza treści dokumentów ani jakości.
Nie wykonuje kodu wskazanego w dowodach. Testy tego skryptu i silnika nie są benchmarkiem LabVIEW.

Raport porównawczy uruchamia się z **zaakceptowanego drzewa**, podając oba katalogi:

```sh
python3 policy/evaluator/evaluate.py --baseline /accepted --candidate /candidate
```

Obsługiwane są też `BASELINE_DIR` i `CANDIDATE_DIR`. Ostatnia linia to JSON zgodny z
kontraktem silnika. Raport zawiera oba stany; błędne dowody kandydata dają `rejected`,
pozostałe przypadki `inconclusive`, zawsze `improved: false`. Nawet komplet odnośników
nie oznacza gotowości benchmarku. `tool_quality: null`, `benchmark_executed: false` oraz
`benchmark_ready: false` pozostają jawne. Raport jest pomocą dla właściciela; przy bramce
`owner` silnik nie uruchamia go automatycznie i nie wykorzystuje go do automatycznego przyjęcia.
Brak pomiaru pozostaje brakiem pomiaru, także po usunięciu lub wymianie indeksu.

Indeks `benchmark/preparation.json` powstanie podczas pracy pętli. Wzór, nie gotowy benchmark:

```json
{"schema_version":1,"milestones":{"sources":[],"tasks":[],"oracle":[],"split":[],"coverage":[],"baseline":[],"challenges":[]}}
```

Każda lista zawiera wpisy `{"path":"benchmark/protocol.md","sha256":"<64 znaki SHA256>"}`.
Dowody muszą być plikami w drzewie, bez symlinków, do 2 MB każdy; duże dane opisuje mały
rekord z przypiętym źródłem i hashem. Sekcje i liczba odnośników służą nawigacji, nie punktacji.
Check działa tylko dla zmian pracy; ścieżki polityki/audytu/dziennika omijają go zgodnie
z silnikiem. Weryfikator sam uruchamia testy każdej zmiany evaluatora.

## Co musi powstać przed implementacją

Pętla przygotuje następujące dowody, następnie niezależny weryfikator sprawdzi metodę,
a właściciel oceni jej wiarygodność przed przyjęciem implementacji. Nie wystarczy utworzyć pliki.

| Obszar | Wymagane ustalenia i dowody |
|---|---|
| sources | Pochodzenie, licencja, commit i SHA256 oryginałów; zależności, wersja zapisu artefaktu i wersja środowiska odczytu osobno. Zachować oryginał przed konwersją. |
| tasks | Zadania o przepływie danych, typach, strukturach, zależnościach, projektach i znaczeniu zmian; ocenialna odpowiedź i wskazanie źródła w oryginale. |
| oracle | Odpowiedzi ustalone niezależnie od czytnika: diagramy i właściwości w LabVIEW, kontrolowane wejścia/wyjścia, dokumentacja, raporty różnic i zapis niezależnej kontroli. Sam eksport badanego narzędzia nie jest wzorcem. |
| split | Rozdział rozwoju i oceny według całych projektów i rodzin; wykrywanie kopii/wariantów. Nowe własne przypadki ograniczają ryzyko znajomości publicznych przykładów przez model. Klucz i część oceniająca poza dostępem badanego agenta; w publicznym repo nie da się ukryć ich samą ścieżką. Przed pomiarem sprawdzić faktyczną izolację. |
| coverage | Inwentaryzacja wszystkich rodzin, wersji, modułów i warunków dostępu; pokrycie jawne, bez usuwania trudnych przypadków z mianownika. Pierwszy zestaw nie redefiniuje celu. |
| baseline | Powtarzalne porównanie tych samych zadań bez narzędzia, z obrazami gdy dostępne, oraz z narzędziem; ten sam model, prompt i budżet, przypięte wersje, powtórzenia, koszt i czas. |
| challenges | Próby metody na celowo błędnych odpowiedziach, błędnych wskazaniach źródła, stałym/pustym eksporcie i nieobsługiwanym przypadku. Zero wykonanych testów, brak runtime lub klucza nie dają zaliczenia. |

Początkowa inwentaryzacja obejmuje VI (panel i diagram), kontrolki i typedefy, biblioteki,
klasy, projekty i build specs, testy, zasoby, zależności, pakiety, skompilowane dystrybucje
oraz warianty modułów i targetów; lista pozostaje otwarta. Wyniki mają osobne przekroje
według rodziny, wersji zapisu i środowiska. Nieprzebadana wersja ma brak pokrycia.
Wariant 2024 wolno wybrać dopiero po przedstawieniu dodatkowego nakładu dla wszystkich
wersji i ograniczeń zgodności, zgodnie z celem; ten setup nie wybiera wariantu zapasowego.

Przyszły raport oddzieli wierność odczytu od poprawności odpowiedzi agentów i ich poparcia
w źródle. Wskaże liczbę zaplanowanych i rzeczywiście wykonanych przypadków oraz wyniki
poprawne, częściowe, nieobsługiwane, brak zależności/licencji/środowiska, chroniony/usunięty
diagram i błąd narzędzia. Uczciwe zgłoszenie ograniczenia nie dowodzi pełnego odczytu.
Sprawdzenie struktury bez sprzętu nie potwierdza zachowania na sprzęcie. Tolerancje,
niedeterminizm i przedziały niepewności trzeba określić przed porównaniem. Nie agregować
tych wymiarów do arbitralnego jednego wyniku ani nie przyjmować progu sukcesu bez właściciela.

## Niezależna kontrola zmian

Evaluator zmienia tylko uprawniona rola, na zlecenie Policymakera. Silnik wymaga odrębnej
sesji weryfikatora i przypina jej zgodę do commita i drzewa evaluatora. Stara wersja
obowiązuje do wyniku `pass`; zmieniony snapshot wymaga ponownej kontroli.
Instrukcje weryfikatora, wspólny kontrakt roli i protokół są chronione w `engine.yml`.
Silnik blokuje też zmianę/usunięcie wpisu `evaluator-verifier` w profilach, zachowując
możliwość tworzenia pozostałych ról. Zmiana tych zabezpieczeń należy do właściciela.
Niezależność oznacza osobną sesję i dowody, nie gwarancję bezbłędności modelu; przy
niepewności weryfikator odmawia `pass`. To nie bramka końcowego sukcesu; jej odroczenie
i wymagane potwierdzenie właściciela zapisano w `goal/goal.md` w temacie D.

## Historical reports

Policymaker and shaper sessions receive actual trusted marked reports in `.session/reports/`.
Find relevant work through `.session/history/manifest.json`; read selected reports.
Use `reports/index.json` to distinguish current reports from pinned evidence when needed.
Each report JSON has `issue`, `source` (comment URL), `snapshot`
(SHA-256 of `body`) and the full `body`. An untrusted author's marker does not qualify.


## The task graph (shaper and Policymaker only)

The shaper writes `.session/tasks.json`; the engine creates the issues and the blocking edges. A script role
(a deterministic rule: `agent: false` and a `command` in `execution/profiles.yml`, named by `shaper` in
`policy/params.yml`) writes the same file and exits 0; a missing or invalid file fails the iteration. The Policymaker writes its orders in the same format to `.session/orders.json`, with an optional `"wake": true` (run again after the ordered tasks end).

```json
{"tasks": [
  {"id": "...", "title": "...", "role": "...", "model": "...", "effort": "...",
   "body": "## Goal\n...\n## Acceptance\n- [ ] ...\n## Verification\n`python3 check.py`\n## Context\n- link: why go there\n## Budget\n- file-or-issue by name",
   "blocked_by": ["..."], "start_branch": "...", "limits": {"timeout_minutes": "...", "max_turns": "..."},
   "inputs": ["..."],
   "exports": [{"source": "...", "iterations": ["..."], "sessions": ["..."]}],
   "consent": {"what": "...", "why": "...", "secrets": ["..."]}}
]}
```

`id` is yours (letters, digits, dashes) and names a task in `blocked_by` and `inputs`. `role` must have a profile.
The `"..."` values are placeholders, not types: `limits` values, `iterations` and `sessions` are integers
(`"limits": {"timeout_minutes": 20}`), `start_branch` is a branch name or null; it must exist on origin when the graph is
submitted. A closed task's `task/N` branch is deleted, but naming it still works while its unmerged work is kept as
the tag `iter/NNNN/N`: the session then starts from that tag.
`model` and `effort` are optional (omitted: the role's default); `model` is an alias (a key of `models`, never a model id) from `policy/params.yml`, and `limits` never exceed the ceilings there. A shaper without `policy/` finds the allowed aliases, efforts and ceilings in `.session/loop-state.json` under `task_options`, and what each role does in `.session/capabilities.json`. A graph or order naming anything else is refused whole; the Policymaker sees a refused order as `orders_refused` of that iteration in `loop-state.json`. `consent` is optional: the
engine asks the owner by itself when a role's profile is beyond the accepted limits. `consent.secrets` lists the names
(`^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$`, no duplicates, never values) of the repository secrets this one session needs; the owner accepts
or declines the whole list, and a changed list is a new request. The width of the iteration is the
widest layer of the graph; it is computed, not a field. Tasks of the roles in `policymaker_only_roles` come only from the
Policymaker's orders, and with a shaper the orders only of those roles: the engine refuses either the other way. Every task fits **one
session**.

`## Verification` is run by the session itself before it reports `done` and again by the engine afterwards, so it must be
runnable with the role's tools. The default tools allow Bash only as `git …`, `python3 …`, `echo`, `printf` or `mkdir`: write one plain command, with no redirection,
`$(…)`, pipes or `test`. Checking a file's content: `python3 -c "import sys; sys.exit(open('src/a.txt').read() != 'text\n')"`.

To consume an artifact produced by another task in this graph, add
`{"from": "producer-id", "name": "weights.bin"}` to `inputs` and the same
`producer-id` to `blocked_by`. Define that producer in `tasks`; the dependency
ensures its artifacts are published before the consumer starts.

`exports` stages supported data for any role, fetched by the engine before the session
starts. Select `streams`, `actions`, `records` or `reports` and explicit integer
`iterations` or `sessions` (issue numbers); both selectors mean their intersection.
`records` supports iteration scope only. Read `.session/exports/manifest.json` for
each result and staged path: `downloaded`, `unavailable`, `expired`, `error`, or
`unknown`. Unknown sources produce `unknown` and execute nothing. A missing
selector keeps the audit's existing stream window (current iteration and three
predecessors); `exports: []` opts out. Other roles have no implicit exports.
